sentences.text:
This is the first bail application filed by the applicant under Section 439 of Cr.P.C. for grant of regular bail relating to FIR No.02/2023 dated 2.1.2023, registered at Police Station - Madhavnagar,
District Katni for the offence under Sections 363, 366, 376(2)(n) of IPC and under Sections 3,4 5(L),
6 of POCSO Act.

He is in detention since 14.01.2023.
2.
A s per the prosecution story on 02.01.2023 prosecutrix's mother lodged an FIR about her 17 years old daughter missing from home.
FIR was registered for commission of offence under Section 363 of IPC on 14.01.2023.
Prosecutrix was recovered by the police and was handed over to her father.
After investigation charge-sheet has been filed for above said offences.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the applicant has submitted that applicant has not committed any offence.
He is innocent.
He has been falsely implicated.
Applicant was having love affair with the prosecutrix but prosecutrix had not gone with him.
He has not committed rape/ aggravated penetrative sexual assault upon the prosecutrix.
It is further submitted that prosecutrix has been examined before the trial Court.
She has not supported the prosecution story.
Therefore, it has been prayed that applicant be released on bail.
4. On the other hand, learned counsel for the State has opposed grant of bail.
5. At the time of alleged incident prosecutrix was 17 years and 10 months old.
In her evidence before the trial Court, she has not supported the prosecution story.

Therefore, having taken into consideration all the facts and circumstances of the case but without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, I am of the view that it is case in which further pre trial detention of the applicant is not warranted.
Consequently, this first bail application under Section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure for grant of bail filed on behalf of applicant, stands allowed 6.

It is directed that applicant - Ajju @ Ajit Sing be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty thousand only) with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court, for his regular appearance before the trial Court during trial with a condition that he shall remain present before the concerned Court on all the dates fixed by it during trial.

He shall abide by all the conditions enumerated under Section 437(3) of Cr.P.C.
7.
This order shall be effective till the end of the trial.
However, in case o f bail jump and breach of any of the conditions of bail, it shall become ineffective.
Certified copy as per rules.

(DINESH KUMAR PALIWAL) JUDGE RC Ajju @Ajit Singh Thakur vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 21 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/199884984/
